Evan Cole: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands runtime section. Dropping a few clarifying Qs so PMs/Eng can act.

Priya Desai: Happy to take kernel + cache. Maya and Tom can cover schedule and batching.

Evan Cole: 1) Will kernel-v4 be opt-in per-tenant or a global default flip? Customers want control.

Maya Torres: We're doing per-region/tenant opt-in first. Console will have a "canary channel" toggle in June; global default flip only after at least two region canaries and a 48-72h stability window. No silent global upgrades.

Zoe Park: For Dedicated customers on reserved capacity, any forced switchover concerns?

Priya Desai: No forced switchover. Dedicated gets extended opt-in and a fallback binary for 90 days. We'll also provide a compatibility shim for KV layout if needed.

Evan Cole: 2) Batching default: 20ms vs 50ms — which should Console recommend for new apps?

Tom Alvarez: Recommend presets: interactive -> 20ms & target_tokens 64; throughput -> 50ms & target_tokens 512. We're adding both knobs to Console and planning an adaptive mode (opt-in) that widens under sustained queue depth. Adaptive will have p99 guardrails.

Evan Cole: 3) KV cache eviction — customers reported warm prefixes dropping after short idle periods. New defaults?

Priya Desai: Moving to segmented LRU with a small pinned segment for prefixes. Defaults: max_entries=100k, pinned_ratio=0.04, idle_ttl_ms=600000 (10m) for non-pinned. Tenants can call `cache.pin=true` per session to preserve prefixes; Console will show pinned counts.

Maya Torres: Timeline: Console toggles and pin UI in mid-May, canary start late May, per-region opt-in in June, global default flip targeted late July pending metrics.

infra-bot: Created task RUNTIME-6721: publish kernel-v4 canary schedule (owner: Maya).

Evan Cole: Action items: Maya publish schedule + rollback steps, Priya update docs with cache examples, Tom publish adaptive-batching guardrails. I'll collate for the all-hands recap. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
